subject: Pricing & Batching follow-up — token volumes / $/1M / continuous batching assumptions
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acmecorp.com>, Ben Owens <ben.owens@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Thanks for the call — next steps on pricing & batching

Hi Sarah / Ben —

Thanks for the thoughtful call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can size a cost estimate that maps to your workload: 

Recap of what we heard:
- Primary use: in-product AI assistant for knowledge base + short summaries (mostly 256–512 token responses).
- Traffic shape: steady 7x/day active users, a large tail of infrequent users. Peak concurrency ~120 requests/minute during product spikes.
- Expected growth: ramp to ~500k monthly active users in 12 months (very approximate).
- Required SLOs: P95 latency <300ms for critical flows.

Questions we need answered (for $/1M token estimate):
1) Estimated monthly token volume (input+output) — please confirm a low/expected/high range.
2) Target budget range for inference (monthly) — helps us recommend hosted vs. dedicated.
3) Acceptable batching window / latency allowance for non-critical flows (e.g., can you accept 150–300ms extra for batching gains?)

Attached: a short CSV template to fill with token estimates and a sample $/1M calculation we use.

Proposed next steps:
- You fill the CSV with low/expected/high token scenarios (if you can get this to us today, we’ll turn around a unit economics table).
- Marissa (cc'd) will validate concurrency/batching assumptions and propose a continuous-batching profile.
- We schedule a 30-min follow-up tomorrow to review the cost model.

Thanks — excited to make this concrete.

—Camila
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai
[Attachment: acme_monthly_token_estimates.csv (csv)]

From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acmecorp.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Owens <ben.owens@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-06-25T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks for the call — next steps on pricing & batching

Camila — thanks, this is great. Attaching our rough token estimates (low/expected/high) and a short note on patterns. Quick answers: 

- Monthly token volumes (input+output): low=80M, expected=320M, high=1.2B. See attached CSV.
- Budget: currently piloting with a monthly inference budget target of $6k–$12k; if ROI looks good, we can expand.
- Latency tolerance: for the assistant UI we need sub-400ms end-to-end; for async summary jobs (nightly batch) we can accept higher latency. For UI flows, max extra batching latency we can accept is ~150ms.
- Concurrency: typical steady-state ~30–60 reqs/min, spike to 120–150 reqs/min for short windows (a few minutes).

We attached the CSV and a short note. Hoping Marissa can advise whether continuous batching at those concurrency levels is realistic for the economy you're showing.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Lee
Product Manager, AcmeCorp
[Attachment: acme_monthly_token_estimates.csv (csv)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acmecorp.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-25T12:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks for the call — next steps on pricing & batching

Thanks for the numbers, Sarah — very helpful. High-level notes on unit economics and continuous batching assumptions: 

1) Unit economics framing:
- Our sample $/1M tokens baseline (hosted, gpt-3.x equiv) for 256–512 token responses is approximately $X/1M tokens at conservative throughput; with continuous batching we typically see 20–45% token price improvement depending on request size distribution and KV cache hit-rate.
- For your expected profile (320M/mo, median response ~320 tokens), we expect sustained batching benefits because many requests share common prefixes and short context windows.

2) Continuous batching assumptions and concurrency:
- Continuous batching works best when steady traffic exists; we maintain a moving window (50–200ms) to group incoming requests on the same device/route. For your steady-state of 30–60 reqs/min, gains are modest but noticeable.
- During spikes (120–150 reqs/min) we can increase batch size and see peak efficiency. The key is tail latency: to keep P95 <300–400ms we recommend a per-request max queuing budget of 100–150ms for UI-critical flows.
- If you need stricter latency (<250ms P95), we can lower the batching window but you'll lose some cost efficiency.

3) Example back-of-envelope for your expected tier (320M/mo):
- Without batching / small batch: baseline cost ~ $Y per 1M tokens.
- With continuous batching (expected): effective cost drops to ~ $Y*0.75–0.85 per 1M tokens.
- Dedicated capacity pricing starts to make sense above ~700M–1B tokens depending on commitment term and desired latency SLOs.

4) Next steps from my side:
- I’ll run your CSV through a quick unit-econ script and share a per-scenario $/1M tokens table and a concurrency/batching profile by flow.
- If you’re open, we can run a 48-hour smoke test on hosted to measure real-world batching efficiency with a small sample of traffic.

Looping in Aditya for any deeper infra-level sizing comments (cc).

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
[Attachment: redwood-pricing-sample-1M.md (markdown)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Ben Owens <ben.owens@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-06-25T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks for the call — next steps on pricing & batching

Quick infra note from my side:

- For the traffic pattern described (median token ~320, 320M/mo expected), hosted with continuous batching should achieve the cost multipliers Marissa mentioned. Key knobs: per-route batching window, KV cache configuration, and model quantization/variant.
- Concurrency/throughput sizing: expect ~12–16k tokens/sec sustained for the expected tier; peak provisioning should handle ~2–3x of steady for short bursts (we can do autoscale but will surface brief latency increases during scale up).
- If Acme wants guaranteed P95 <300ms at all times under your high scenario, recommend Dedicated with reserved pools and a small hot standby buffer — pricing will shift to a commitment model but gives predictable latency.

I'll prepare a short slide with three scenarios (hosted with batching, hosted without batching, dedicated) and include $/1M token numbers for low/expected/high. Can share by EOD.

Thanks — happy to jump on the follow-up meeting.

—Aditya
